tasks.title: Merging netplan files
tasks.statement: Write a function netplan_merge(files): files is a list of triples [directory, file name, configuration], where the configuration is already-parsed YAML (a dictionary like {'network': {...}}). These are the rules of netplan generate. Only files whose name ends in .yaml from the directories /lib/netplan, /etc/netplan and /run/netplan count (ignore other directories and names). If the same file name occurs in several directories, only the file from the highest-priority directory stays: /run/netplan is above /etc/netplan, which is above /lib/netplan; the other files of that name are dropped entirely. The remaining files are processed in order of their names (names are compared as plain strings, the directory does not matter): a later file is added to the accumulated result. Merging two values: two dictionaries are merged key by key, recursively, by the same rules; two lists are concatenated (the new items are appended to the old list); in all other cases (numbers, strings, booleans, different types) the new value replaces the old one. Return the final configuration (an empty dictionary if there are no files).
tasks.hint: First a dictionary name -> (directory, config) with priorities, then sorted(names) and a recursive merge(a, b).

tasks.title: From netplan to a .network file
tasks.statement: Write a function netplan_to_networkd(name, definition): name is the netplan ID of an Ethernet device, definition is its dictionary. Return the text of the .network file that a simplified model of the networkd renderer would build. The sections go in this order and are separated by exactly one blank line, the text ends with a single newline; empty sections are not written. 1) [Match]: if match is present, in order the lines Name=<match.name>, MACAddress=<match.macaddress in lowercase>, Driver=<match.driver> (only those that are set); with no match, one line Name=<name>. 2) [Link] with the line MTUBytes=<mtu> if mtu is set. 3) [Network]: a DHCP= line with yes if both dhcp4 and dhcp6 are on, ipv4 if only dhcp4, ipv6 if only dhcp6, otherwise no; then an Address=<address> line for each item of addresses; then DNS=<address> for each nameservers.addresses; then one Domains= line with the words of nameservers.search separated by spaces, if the list is not empty. 4) One [Route] section per item of routes, in order: Destination=<to>, where a to equal to default becomes 0.0.0.0/0 (or ::/0 if via contains a colon); then Gateway=<via> if via is set; then Metric=<metric> if metric is set. The on-link field is not modelled. 5) [DHCPv4] if dhcp4-overrides has use-dns and/or route-metric: UseDNS=yes or no, then RouteMetric=<number>.
tasks.hint:
Build a list of sections, each a list of lines, and finish with '

'.join('
'.join(s) ...) + '
'.

tasks.title: Parsing nmcli -t
tasks.statement: Write a function parse_nmcli_terse(text): text is the output of nmcli -t -f NAME,UUID,TYPE,DEVICE connection show. In -t mode the fields are separated by a colon, and a colon or a backslash inside a value is escaped with a backslash (\: and \\). Skip empty and whitespace-only lines, and lines that do not give exactly four fields after splitting. For every other line return a tuple (name, uuid, type, device) with the escaping already removed: replace the type 802-3-ethernet with ethernet and 802-11-wireless with wifi (keep other types as they are); replace an empty device with None (the profile is not active). Keep the order of the lines.
tasks.hint: Walk the characters: a backslash takes the next character literally, an unescaped colon closes the field.

tasks.title: A .nmconnection profile
tasks.statement: Write a function parse_keyfile(text): text is the content of a NetworkManager profile in keyfile format (ini: sections in square brackets, key=value lines; skip lines starting with # and empty lines; strip spaces around the key and the value; a repeated key in a section replaces the previous one). Return a dictionary with the keys: id - connection.id (or ''); type - connection.type with 802-3-ethernet replaced by ethernet and 802-11-wireless by wifi (or ''); interface - connection.interface-name (or ''); autoconnect - False only if connection.autoconnect equals false (case-insensitive), otherwise True; method4 - ipv4.method (if the key is missing, 'auto'); addresses - the list of addresses from the addressN keys of the ipv4 section (N is an integer, order by ascending N, not by text position), in each value the address/prefix comes before the first comma; gateway - the value of the gateway key of the ipv4 section, and if it is missing or empty, the gateway after the comma in the first addressN (in order) that has one, otherwise ''; dns - the list of addresses from ipv4.dns (separator ;, drop empty items); routes - a list of tuples (network, gateway, metric) from the routeN keys of the ipv4 section in ascending N: the value is network/prefix[,gateway[,metric]], a missing gateway is '', a missing metric is None, the metric is an integer. Keys such as route1_options and dns-search are neither addressN nor routeN.
tasks.hint: Collect the sections into a dictionary of dictionaries; for addressN and routeN use re.fullmatch(r'address(\d+)', key) and sort by int.

tasks.title: Which .network file applies
tasks.statement: Write a function networkd_pick(units, iface): units is a list of triples [directory, file name, match], iface is a dictionary of interface properties with the keys name, mac, type, driver and possibly managed_by. match is a dictionary of the conditions of the [Match] section (each value is a string; a missing key means no condition; an empty dictionary matches every interface) or None: that is how an empty file or a symlink to /dev/null, which masks a file of the same name, is written. These are the rules of systemd-networkd. Only names ending in .network from the directories /etc/systemd/network, /run/systemd/network and /usr/lib/systemd/network count (ignore the rest). Files with the same name replace each other: the file from the highest-priority directory stays (/etc is above /run, which is above /usr/lib); if the remaining file is a mask (None), it matches no interface. Files are visited in order of their names (plain string comparison), and the first file whose conditions all hold is applied; the others are ignored even if they match. Conditions: Name, Type, Driver - a whitespace-separated list of shell-style globs (fnmatchcase), true if at least one matches; if the value starts with '!', the result of the whole condition is inverted; MACAddress - a whitespace-separated list of addresses, compared case-insensitively, no globs. An interface whose managed_by is set and is not 'io.systemd.Network' matches no file. Return the name of the chosen file, or '' if none matches.
tasks.hint: First keep one file per name (by directory priority), then sorted(names) and check the conditions; for '!' strip the first character and invert the result of any(...).

tasks.title: From ifcfg to keyfile
tasks.statement: Older RHEL-family releases kept profiles in /etc/sysconfig/network-scripts/ifcfg-*; keyfile is the default now. Write a function ifcfg_to_keyfile(text): text is the content of an ifcfg file (lines KEY=value; skip empty lines and lines with #; a value may be in single or double quotes - strip them; strip spaces at the edges). Return a dictionary of sections {section: {key: string}} by a simplified model of the migration. The connection section is always there: id - NAME, or if it is missing or empty, DEVICE (or ''); type - by TYPE: Ethernet -> ethernet, Bond -> bond, Bridge -> bridge, Vlan -> vlan, anything else or missing -> ethernet; interface-name - DEVICE (the key is written only if DEVICE is non-empty); autoconnect with the value 'false' only if ONBOOT equals no (case-insensitive) (the default is ONBOOT=yes, the key is not written). The ethernet section is written only if it has something in it: mac-address - HWADDR as is, mtu - MTU as is (a string). The ipv4 section is always there: if BOOTPROTO equals dhcp (case-insensitive) - method=auto; otherwise if IPADDR is set - method=manual, address1=IPADDR/prefix (the prefix is PREFIX, or if absent the length of the mask in NETMASK; if that is absent too - 32) and gateway=GATEWAY if GATEWAY is set; otherwise method=disabled. Regardless of the method, if there are keys DNS1, DNS2, ... (any number after DNS, in ascending numeric order, skip empty values), add dns - the addresses joined by ; with a trailing ;.
tasks.hint: The mask length is ipaddress.ip_network('0.0.0.0/' + mask).prefixlen; select the DNS keys with re.fullmatch(r'DNS\d+', key).

tasks.title: Two owners for one NIC
tasks.statement: Write a function find_conflicts(networkctl, nmcli, interfaces): three texts - the output of networkctl list (header IDX LINK TYPE OPERATIONAL SETUP, then lines of five words and a final N links listed. line), the output of nmcli device status (columns DEVICE TYPE STATE CONNECTION aligned with the header; STATE and CONNECTION values may contain spaces) and the file /etc/network/interfaces. Work out who claims each interface. networkd claims it if SETUP is configured or configuring. NetworkManager claims it if STATE is connected or starts with connecting (connected (externally) is a configuration done by something else, it does not count). ifupdown claims it if the name is listed on an auto or allow-hotplug line (one or more names follow the word) and there is at least one iface name family method line for it with a method other than manual; ignore text after #. Ignore the interface lo completely. Return a dictionary {interface: sorted list of claimants (the names networkd, NetworkManager, ifupdown)} only for interfaces claimed by two or more.
tasks.hint: The nmcli column positions come from re.finditer(r'\S+', header); a column's value is the slice of the line from its start to the start of the next column.

tasks.title: Validating bond, bridge and VLAN
tasks.statement: Write a function validate_netplan(cfg): cfg is parsed netplan YAML {'network': {...}} with optional sections ethernets, bonds, bridges, vlans (dictionaries ID -> definition; a section may be missing or None). Return a sorted list, without duplicates, of error strings by the checker's rules (the exact text matters). 1) version is not 2 or is missing: 'network: version must be 2'. 2) For each member of the interfaces of a bond or bridge that is not defined in any of the four sections: 'bonds.<id>: member <name> is not defined' (for a bridge 'bridges.<id>: ...'). 3) A bond's mode is parameters.mode (default balance-rr); valid ones are balance-rr, active-backup, balance-xor, broadcast, 802.3ad, balance-tlb, balance-alb, otherwise 'bonds.<id>: unknown mode <mode>'. 4) If the mode is valid but not 802.3ad and parameters has lacp-rate: 'bonds.<id>: lacp-rate only applies to mode 802.3ad'. 5) For each VLAN: id must be an integer from 0 to 4094, otherwise 'vlans.<id>: id <value> out of range 0-4094' (a missing id is printed as None); a missing link gives 'vlans.<id>: link is required', an undefined one 'vlans.<id>: link <name> is not defined'. 6) A device listed in interfaces of two or more different bonds/bridges: '<name>: member of more than one aggregate (<IDs in alphabetical order joined by comma and space>)'. 7) A member device with a non-empty addresses or dhcp4/dhcp6 turned on: '<name>: member of <first aggregate alphabetically> must not have addresses or dhcp'. A member's definition is looked up in all four sections.
tasks.hint: First a dictionary of all definitions and a dictionary member -> set of aggregates, then the checks one by one; finish with sorted(set(errs)).

tasks.title: How netplan try ends
tasks.statement: Write a function try_outcome(old, new, ssh_addr, client, confirm_at, timeout): a model of netplan try. old and new are the configurations before and after the change as {interface: {'addresses': [CIDR, ...], 'gateway': an address or missing}}; ssh_addr is the IPv4 address of the server to which your SSH session is connected (no prefix); client is the IPv4 address of your computer; confirm_at is the second at which you will press confirm, or None if you will not; timeout is the wait in seconds. After new is applied, the session stays alive only if both conditions hold: ssh_addr is (without the prefix) in addresses of some interface of new, and client either lies in the subnet of one of the addresses of any interface of new, or some interface of new has a non-empty gateway. If the session is alive, confirm_at is not None and confirm_at <= timeout, the change is confirmed: return the tuple ('kept', confirm_at, a copy of new). Otherwise the configured network is rolled back: return ('rolled back', timeout, a copy of old).
tasks.hint: ipaddress.ip_interface('192.0.2.10/24').network gives the subnet; ip_address(client) in subnet tests membership.
